Dead by Daylight is basically a fun anxiety simulator where you try to fix generators and try to escape while a killer with Olympic-level tracking skills comes running after you. Like how are they so good at being the killer?!?!? whenever I be the killer, its simply a free win for the survivors. I'd be running around looking in the other part of the map while the players are escaping. Every match feels like a comedy sketch, someone’s hiding in a bush thinking they’re invisible, someone else is looping the killer like they’re auditioning for Fast & Furious, and you’re probably running in the wrong direction the entire time. Half the game is screaming or if you're not the type to scream (like me, ahem ahem) your heart will be racing because the killer is chasing you or is near you, the other half is laughing at how badly things went lol. It’s chaotic, fun, and for certain players it keeps you on your toes, but in the end no matter how you feel, somehow you just can’t stop pressing “ready up”. The thrill it provides is really great xD.

Its unique asymmetrical gameplay, where one player takes on the role of a terrifying killer and others try to escape, creates intense and thrilling moments. The game’s atmosphere is hauntingly immersive, with great graphics and sound design that heighten the suspense. With a variety of killers, survivors, and maps, Dead by Daylight offers endless replayability and fun for horror fans. It’s a must-try for anyone who loves adrenaline-pumping multiplayer experiences!

Dead by Daylight is one of those games that sticks with you—fast-paced, intense, and full of moments that get your heart racing. Whether you’re playing Survivor or Killer, every match feels different thanks to the unique characters, perks, maps, and unpredictable players you go up against.

If you like games with strategy, teamwork, and clutch moments, DBD delivers hard. Survivors have to outsmart the killer, manage objectives, and stay calm under pressure, while Killers get the thrill of hunting, predicting moves, and mastering their powers. It’s super rewarding once you learn the mechanics, and the skill ceiling keeps it interesting even after hundreds of hours.

The devs constantly add new content—new killers, survivors, perks, and events—so the game doesn’t get stale. And honestly, some of the character designs and lore are just too good. Whether you want a competitive experience or just chaotic, funny matches with friends, DBD is perfect.

If you’re looking for a multiplayer game that’s scary, strategic, and hella fun with friends, I definitely recommend giving Dead by Daylight a try. Just be ready for adrenaline, mind games, and some salty lobbies.

Let's talk about the lore, which is, frankly, the most hilarious part of this whole experience.

We are all trapped by a cosmic, malevolent entity known only as The Entity. 

Think of it as a giant, unknowable spider-god that lives in another dimension and feeds on hope and despair.

This explains everything:Why we repair generators only to escape and do it again: The Entity is running the most poorly-managed, never-ending electrician apprenticeship in the multiverse. It needs those little bursts of hope (fixing the gen) and the despair (getting hooked right after) to sustain itself. It’s basically a drama llama on a cosmic scale.

The Campfire: After a truly miserable trial where a Killer tunneled you out in $5$ minutes, you return to the campfire. This is where you and the Killer sit in awkward silence, sharing a cold can of beans while The Entity silently judges your performance. ("Dwight, that 360 was pathetic. Not enough despair. Try harder next time.")

The Killers: They are all victims of this cosmic being, forced to murder forever. Except for maybe Michael Myers. He just followed his sister into a different dimension because he felt like it. He's the only one who doesn't seem to notice the giant spider-god. Legend.

The Items: The Entity provides survivors with flashlights and med-kits. Why? Because the Entity is a benevolent host who wants you to have a fighting chance... so the despair is sweeter when you inevitably lose your rare Styptic Agent to a camping Bubba. It's the ultimate emotional roller coaster designed by a celestial teenager.Final Verdict: This game is a terrifying, fun, and deeply meta commentary on video game addiction, where the real final boss is the feeling of obligation to grind 2 million Bloodpoints. The Entity is a genius villain who makes sure every game is just annoying enough that you want revenge, but never so annoying that you uninstall.

10/10 – Must Buy. Don't worry about escaping; you're not going anywhere.

This is a problematic review in so far as the game it self is fun/enjoyable as both a survivor and as a killer (caveat that I play both and do so with randoms only -- no pre-made teams by design).

The balance in the game is questionable. Depending on skill levels, perks, which killer, which map and which map iteration etc. the balance can be substantively skewed to one faction or another. This is, largely, intrinsic to the game.

The studio, as a general rule, does not seem to actually listen to the player base and often does streams espousing various metrics as the basis for their decision making processes. However, the neutrality of the data collection and it's interpretation is highly suspect (the last survey had a single section for killer input with the rest of the survey -- being survivor centric only). If I make a survey for for a school which asks the question "Do you want to get out of school 60 minutes early every day?" It would be highly likely that the majority would vote yes. However, if it was not disclosed that, in getting out early every day, that all school sports would be cancelled as there would no longer be sufficient time in the day to conduct them, then the poll results would likely change as the question would no longer be misleading.

Misleading data collection skews the data. A desired outcome, when present prior to data analysis, skews said analysis. Behaviour Interactive seems to have a long history of making data fit their desired narative. This is, at best, disingenuous and tone deaf.

The questionable paradigm of Behaviour Interactive Inc. notwithstanding the other major issue with Dead by Daylight is the community.

There is substantive toxicity here -- both as survivours and as killers. There are times that Dead by Daylight could readily give Rust a run for it's money in the toxicity category. There are many good players as well -- helpful, polite et al. Good teamwork and skilled killers. There are also a great number of individuals who seem to be overcompensating for diminutive genitalia (irrespective of age, gender or socio-economic status).

This is a good game with a good community and an above average demographic of very "LOUD" toxic players.

Is this game worth a buy -- when things are on sale yes.

Get what interests you and then get what is borderline via free in game currency (you get shards as you level up and can unlock many things for free beyond the time spent playing to get to that point). Do not, however, buy this title expecting every run to be amiable -- people will rub you the wrong way with above average regularity and the development team will frustrate  you with bias and tone-deaf responses the majority of the time.

Dead by Daylight delivers a level of tension that few multiplayer games can match. Every match raises my heartbeat, especially during chases and loops, and the overall atmosphere consistently keeps me on edge. When the game is running smoothly, the blend of teamwork, stealth, and mind games is genuinely exciting.

The downside is that the experience is highly inconsistent. The game still suffers from frequent bugs, and the presence of hackers can ruin matches outright. New or inexperienced teammates often make the experience frustrating on both sides, whether you queue as killer or survivor. With no in-game communication, coordinating as survivors is challenging, and a single weak link can collapse the entire match structure.

In my experience, about half of the matches feel balanced and enjoyable. The other half are either heavily one-sided or disrupted by teammates who troll, disconnect, or even assist the killer. These situations undermine the competitive tension that makes the game compelling.

On the narrative side, Dead by Daylight has surprisingly rich lore. Some characters have well-developed backstories that add depth to the universe, and exploring that side of the game is a nice bonus for players who enjoy world-building.

Overall, the game offers intense, memorable moments, but the quality of the experience varies significantly from match to match. When it works, it is thrilling. When it doesn’t, it can be genuinely frustrating.

Dead by Daylight is a super fun and scary game where you play as either a survivor or a killer. Survivors try to escape and repair generators, while killers hunt them down.

Exciting and intense gameplay.
Lots of killers and survivors with unique abilities.
Regular updates with new content.
Cons:
Killer matchmaking times can be really long.
Some survivors feel overpowered.
Can get a bit repetitive.
Overall: If you love horror games and don’t mind the long wait times, definitely give it a try!

[h1] A review for players (like me) who left and are considering returning. [/h1]

//TLDR: I recommend returning to test the many quality of life improvements they have added. You will likely enjoy re-learning the game and feeling you have a chance (as a survivor or killer) to win. But there are still frustrating things relating to gameplay you may not want to mess with again. Connecting with this old friend will be nostalgic, but as they speak, you’ll slowly realise why you wanted to cut ties in the first place. 
_______________________________________________________________
As an older player (1k+ hours – played both survivor and killer) who took a VERY long break when things were at their WORST, I think I can finally recommend this game again — with a grain of salt. They’ve added a lot of quality-of-life improvements, and the game feels very different now. I’ll mention the changes, then the things to consider.

[b] Survivor [/b]
[list]
[*]Maps have changed, and there are pallets placed near the edges now. So all hope is not lost if you have to run there.
[*]Quick disconnects no longer ruin a match because a bot automatically replaces the player. They’re not perfect, but they’ll do saves and heals. Honestly better than some real players lol
[*]When you’re slugged and dying on the floor, there’s a quick “abandon” button.
[*]There is now a camp timer, so killers can’t facecamp endlessly. (You can escape SECOND STATE if a killer camps too.)
[/list]

[b] Killer [/b]
[list]
[*]The camp timer loads slowly 
[*]Many survivor perks that used to enable bullying are pretty limited now (e.g., Unbreakable is once per trial, Self-Care is very slow, etc.).
[*]Survivor items are toned down. Medkits max out at about 2 full heals (with rare add-ons; usually only 1 heal and slower for self-heal). Toolboxes can’t repair half a gen anymore, etc.
[*]The game is heavily in your favour (maybe too much as you’ll read below lol) 
[/list]

[b] General [/b]
[list]
[*]The bloodweb has an instant-spend button so you don’t have to manually click everything if you don’t want to.
[*]Lobbies load pretty quickly.
[*]You can collect banners and icons now — more rewarding than just bloodpoints and those piece of dust charms 
[*]Maps are a bit smaller, making things more balanced: edge pallets help survivors, smaller areas help killers monitor.
 [*]There’s sometimes the new 2v8 game mode. Like yeah, I don't understand it, but cool to see things happening.
[/list]

[b] Things that still BOTHER ME [/b]
[b] Survivor Issues [/b]
[list]
[*]Vaulting, even with Resilience, still feels useless if the killer is anywhere “near.” They’ll hit you almost every time. I can’t stand this, i’m a skinny girl.
[*]Some killers have ridiculous reach (cough Myers’ lunge, cough Bubba’s never-ending chainsaw). It doesn’t feel like skill — just bad balance.
[*]Throwing down pallets mid-chase is still not easy. Running from one loop to another with bloodlust up? You’ll never reach a pallet and drop it before the killer lunges. They clearly prioritise the hit over giving you the stun prompt in time. Extremely unenjoyable gameplay for a survivor.
[/list]

New killers that get added are still all over the place balance-wise for example
[list]
 [*]Houndmaster – If the dog gets you, you’re slower than walking and have no hope of getting the dog off. There’s no real counterplay, not sure why they pretend it’s an option.
 [*]Chucky – He’s tiny. On dark maps he’s basically invisible. Honestly? He should become a BIG BOI during chase. I can’t believe how unfair he is on darker maps.
[/list]

[b] Killer Issues [/b]
[list]
[*]Some maps have so many pallets now that even mediocre survivors can drop pallets all day and be fine. 
[*]If you accidentally hook two survivors close to each other, you might trigger the camp timer unfairly.
[*]Older killers feel pretty outdated compared to the new ones.
[*]Enclosed maps are an instant “don’t bother with your power” for certain killers who need open space. For example, if you’re on Raccoon City Police Station playing Oni, there’s no point going into your power or you'll just bash walls all day. 
[/list]

ALSOOOO the brightness on some maps is so low?? Can’t seeee… Playing killer in first-person is poo poo. A survivor versing Chucky… wee wee.

[b] BUT OVERALL [/b]

Honestly? The game is fun again — especially with friends. It’s not perfect, but if you left because it felt like actual torture to get into rounds, it might be worth returning just to see the changes. How long you stay again? I’m not sure O_<

For now, I’ve played daily-ish and had fun re-learning the game.
Though at its core, it’s still Dead by Daylight, with only 4 core tasks on either side (gen, unhook, heal, gate… or stalk, chase, hit, hook). Maybe you miss the simplicity. Maybe you’ve moved on to greater things. Either choice is reasonable.

Dead by Daylight is probably one of the most chaotic 4v1 horror games out there, emphasis on the "horror" getting jumped scared it the best part. Survivors must work together repairing generators while the Killer relentlessly chases them down like they owe him lunch money.

If you consider playing Survivor you can expect to panic, miss easy skill checks, or die in a sort span of a few seconds. Of course there's counter play to ever Killer that you'll eventually learn in due time but don't worry, I have nearly 600 hours in the game and I too still run into walls while being chased (It's gotta be the chase music, I swear it's too good.). On the other hand, if you consider playing Killer there's plenty of versatile builds and abilities each killer has that you can to aid you in your ruthless hunt against the Survivors. Both parties have cool and fun builds you can use to either try and befriend each other or make people disconnect because of your pure raw talent at the game.

With all being said the community can be back and forth at times, there's friendly people and there's toxic people. Although, that can be said about a lot of games. You'll have fun or you'll have the worst game of your life that makes you want to get off and uninstall but you'll always come back eventually it's a very addictive game and the Devs are trying to make it better for both parties to have fun. I wouldn't give it a perfect 10/10 but maybe a solid 8/10, I would shake my ass with a map and chase "Hex" names all day long if it means playing this game, it's truly a great experience with friends.

Dead by Daylight is the grandfather of the asymmetrical horror X survivors vs X killer game genre. It is unfortunately uncontested as with many other 'DBD killers' like Texas Chainsaw Massacre, Friday the 13th the game, etc shutting down, DBD remains a mainstay for those who enjoy that type of game. There is a reason I said unfortunately.

Dead by Daylight is a horribly balanced game on both ends, with numerous periods of time where the game has been unplayable for either killer or survivor due to Overpowered perks, items, add-ons, etc. The playerbase is extremely polarized with Killer mains and Survivor mains at each others throat, with an 'us vs them' mentality being extremely prevalent in nearly every space you go in the community as the toxic members of each side only ruin the reputation of their own side.

This isn't helped by the fact that the developers seem to be extremely out of touch with their own game, with broken killers like Blight and ESPECIALLY Nurse remaining unchanged, and needing to have OTHER killers perks balanced around them [i] (Nurse has been unchanged despite being the best killer for [b] 8 YEARS [/b] btw) [/i]. And for the survivor side, there were insta blind flashlights that were BEGGED to be removed for years, they were only removed [b] AFTER THE GAME DIRECTOR PLAYED KILLER AGAINST A TEAM WITH 4 INSTA BLIND FLASHLIGHTS AND GOT BULLIED RELENTLESSLY [/b] with the removal coming a month after that match. Needless to say again, but there is a very good reason why the community jokes that the Devs don't even play their own game.

The only people who hate playing Dead by Daylight more than Dead by Daylight fans are the Dead by Daylight Developers. I only find fun when I'm playing with friends and not taking things seriously, because the moment you do, you realize you could be playing literally anything else and be having more fun.

The worst part is that I don't want this game to die, I would love to see the day that the game is well balanced for both sides and the community stops trying to rip each other apart. But the only way I see that happening is if a 'DBD Killer' actually goes on the market, retains its players, and doesn't shut down within 2 years so Dead by Daylight actually has to try.

Hello Human, here are some notes to help you on your journey of the DEAD BY DAYLIGHT experience:

- Lots of crossovers, allowing you to play as cool characters from many horror universes

- Game naturally creates chaotic scenarios with all the combinations of perks and addons in play (sometimes for good, sometimes for ill)

- Heavy DLC policy, requiring you to purchase characters. Not as important on the survivor side (since the survivors are essentially cosmetic changes), but on the killer side you are much more limited since they have unique powers you are missing out on. Not as expensive as other games with this same model but still not great practice

- Very poor progression, takes a long time to unlock people. Bloodpoints and Bloodweb system is basically just a waste of time that pulls you out of just playing the game (different currency then the one you use to get characters). Get stuck in scenarios where you want to play a character for their abilities/looks but also want to get other characters just for their associated perks. Further made worse by shrine of secrets being very unforgiving (can't just buy perks, need to get them for a high price from a random weekly rotation of 4/200+ perks) and uses the same currency (Iridescent shards) to buy characters, further complicating the process.

- Game controls are not bad but are strange sometimes (they try to keep it only 2 buttons no matter the cost, even if it means creating these weird cycle mode abilities rather then just have it be 3 separate buttons) (seems to be done to simplify controller, at the expense of keyboard). Not a terribly degrading thing just a bit weird to get used to.

- Quite buggy, some characters are in weird broken states for extended periods of time. For instance, one character named the houndmaster has a dog that follows them. There is about a 10%? chance that using your ability to send the dog out just does nothing, this bug has existed for a very long time considering how impactful it is.

- Design wise is in this weird limbo state where it isn't optimal for either causal nor competitive ways of playing. A good example of this is with map design. Many maps are slightly unoptimal to play more competitively since the RNG makes them not always spawn the same, preventing 100% optimization for cool map-knowledge plays. On the other hand, the way that the RNG is implemented is not very interesting (mostly a reshuffling of generic tiles) so casually it feels essentially like the same map. This basically causes a local minima where neither side is completely satisfied. This philosophy extends onto character design, perk design, and base kit design with particular playstyles.

- Adding onto design philosophy, it is also counter-intuitive and punishing in strange ways. On survivor, you have no ability to see your teammates, see your teammates' perks, or communicate to them via text or voice chat in game. This creates a very large disparity between coordinated teams using discord versus uncoordinated teams, further exacerbated by the difference between coordinated perk and add-on usage versus uncoordinated. The game is obscuring information preventing you from working with your team in the team-based game. On killer, the most logical way to win a 1v4 scenario is to remove one person from the equation as fast as possible (known as tunneling) so that it simplifies the game-state in your favor. It makes then the most sense that on survivor that you need to spread out damage across your team so that no one dies too early. The way that it is currently implemented is in such a manner where tunneling isn't really fun to do or go against, but is also in a state where the game is sort of balanced around it. You are punished for killing in the killing game as a killer. It's not impossible for the game to be fun on both sides while balancing around tunneling being the norm (Identity V does this quite well), and I don't believe that it is impossible to have a scenario where tunneling is one of multiple strategies that exist, but the way DBD handles it again puts it in a local minima where neither side really has as much fun doing it as alternative playstyles (if they win in a scenario where they spread out hooks, it doesn't offer them any unique advantage and is not as decisive of a victory as if they just tunneled), but there is some game scenarios where there isn't really an alternative other than just lose immediately. TLDR, there exists aspects of the game that are punishing and not clear, some of which create a circumstance where the path to victory is not congruent with the most fun way of playing.

- Development time on these aforementioned problems as well as just balance changes in general is very slow. Some changes that one would think would be a easy net positive QOL can take years to implement for not very clear reasons. 

Overall, this game has very good potential, but is stunted from questionable design decisions and progression. It is enjoyable on occasion, but you basically need to completely dissassociate from 1. Winning/Losing  2.  Progression and 3. Bugs (just laugh at them),  in order to have consistent fun. As you can see I have followed this game for a while, so I had a lot to say about it (I have about +100 hours not on this account), and can say that my Disassociation Techinque is one of the most effective techniques in all of gaming, perfectly employable in this specific scenario to be used to the upmost advantage. Good luck out their in the fog soldier, or just play Identity V which is free and is advantaged in almost all areas except graphics and horror icon crossovers.

You know, I've had longstanding opinion that PvP games have suffered from the common issue of players and developers alike assuming that bad sportsmanship and the zero-sum nature of the game are both not only inevitable, but necessary factors. Entirely too many people chase the wild goose that is balance, without affording any thought as to whether or not their game would even be fun were they to achieve the impossible. "Have any of them wondered," I ask myself, "if a 50% winrate truly feels like a 50% winrate?"

Games like Dead by Daylight help answer this conundrum for me. Here it is, standing out from the crowd; unlike most other game's I've played, this one is separate from them all, different to its core. It sits me down, leans over, and whispers sweetly into my ears: "You're completely fucking right actually! I hate people." Then it clubs me over the head and offers to sell me a fashionable bandage for $5.

Leave aside the issues of a horrible and punishing new player experience. Leave aside the richly awful new privacy policy. Do not worry yourself about the game's obsession with DLC and microtransactions, or the fact that interesting gameplay alterations are deliberately and pointlessly locked to time-limited events designed to generate a fear-of-missing-out. All of this pales by comparison.

This thing could scarcely be a better tool for engendering bitterness in its playerbase if it had been specifically engineered to do so. Every game, win or lose, ends up feeling like a hurdle that took something from you. The only people who truly thrive in this environment are the kind who specifically come to spit in the face of others—I ask someone why they enjoy playing Survivor, a role I find stressful and impossible, and you know what I was told? "I like to show killers their place." Call me crazy, but I don't think rampant mutual antagonism is a very healthy relationship for players to have with each other.

The role of a game designer is to create a mechanism by which players can explore various emotions. Frustration is a valid one, as games like Getting Over It have proved. But those were deliberate. This? This is callous negligence. As any other review can tell you, the toxicity is rampant. And I can't even blame people for it! How could I, when the game seems designed to [i]teach you[/i] to seek revenge on others and treat them as awfully as possible? I suppose it's at least on-brand for a game about a bunch of merciless bastards, if nothing else.

I feel bad for myself, because of the energy I've lost on games that made my day worse. I feel bad for other players, for having found an environment so rancid it ends up making them venomous just to feel sane. I feel bad for the players who I managed to thoroughly beat, since I know it's likely they had an awful time facing me. And I feel bad for my friends, who hoped that I could have fun playing this; though they too have left negative reviews, so at least I can know they will understand.

Mark my words, this game will never fix itself. Not because it can't be - the concept could be great, if enough work were done to fix it - but because Behavior Interactive is not interested in doing that. They're making money off of people, and that's all that matters. Considering this, and all the pain this game is prone to causing, I can recommend trying this game only in some hypothetical context wherein the publisher loses more money off you than they gain. No game that breeds this much hate deserves to turn a profit.

A word spared for the kind, though: There are a few occasions, and a few players, who when playing Killer will grant you leniency. They will not chase you relentlessly, thus giving you a chance to accomplish something. They will limit how many people they kill, so that at least some survivors can have a win. And especially as a new player, this was wonderful, and win or lose I enjoyed my time with them. Though it can't make up for the tremendous issues embedded in this game's execution, I greatly appreciate their considerate actions.

After probably too many hours more than I would have liked, I have finally broken down and decided to write a review.

First and foremost, I absolutely would never recommend this to anyone to play normal matched of dbd in its current state, the most fun you will ever have in this game is custom matches with friends where nobody is really taking it that seriously or forming certain rivalries between friends, but at the end of it all, you're all friends just having a good time.

There are two things I want to specifically talk about that is the biggest problem for me with dbd in its current state.
The first being the horrendous matchmaking system. Ever since I had a good string of games as killer, every game since then I have went up against multiple thousand hour players and too many p100 players who are way above my skill range. Compared to them, I am pretty much nothing. I don't know even 10% of the game compared to them and every single "good" play I think I have, there will always be one sweaty player making sure that play will go south almost immediately.
Every time I load into a game nowadays I am always met with the sweatiest players that completely ruin the killer experience, and it is extremely demotivating to continue playing killer with several different ways to give a middle finger to killer players.
The overabundance of really strong perks, such as Sprint Burst, Lithe, Vigil, Decisive Strike, Finesse, Deliverance, Unbreakable, Dead Hard, even Saboteur and Background Player can be so infuriating to go against every. single. match.
These perks would be fine if only a certain handful of people were using them, but no you see pretty much the same builds or a certain few perks everywhere and it leads to the same exact matches every single time.
And yes I understand that survivor players want to use the best perks, who wouldn't in any other game, but it compounds with the general gameplay changes as well that just make playing killer near impossible unless you have 1k+ hours.

The second point is just how much leeway the survivor side as a whole has been given in the past few updates, specifically the Pallet Density update.
The point of pallets and dead zones was knowing how many resources you had and how to best use them for you and your team, now with there being 3x as many pallets you really don't need to care about which ones you throw since you can walk 5 feet and see another pallet and loop to fully utilize, killing even more time for the killer that can only really be ignored by the highest tiered killers.

Take, for example, the suggested slugging changes, if the survivors were never letting you hook you would think the best course of action would be to just slug them all and then start hooking, but with this change that wouldn't even work since once you tried that everyone would be able to pick themselves back up and every single play that you try to make that you think can give yourself the upper hand just doesn't work, putting you into a situation where every play you do is a losing situation.

Killers always seem to get the short end of the stick since survivors are able to make mistake after mistake and still be completely fine from their perks and pallets, whereas killers can make one early mistake and the entire game is doomed to fail. This doesn't sit right with me.

For me, 2v8 and Custom games are perfectly fine.
But why exactly.

2v8 is so much more relaxed on both sides, since there are no individual perks for the survivors, only perk sets, and the stress of being the only one making mistakes is alleviated since you have a SECOND killer to help.
With there being no overly powerful perk sets for the survivors, it is much more manageable to deal with as a killer, and with the sheer number of survivors it is also easy enough to do your objectives since you have about 2 people being chased at any given time and about 4-6 people working on generators. This in itself is perfectly fine, and I love playing 2v8 on both sides, if I play killer, I play with a friend and have fun, and when I play survivor, I either play solo or with the same friend since we are playing survivor while we wait for the killer queue, and both are extremely fun no matter if I die or escape.

And custom games, as I said before, are very relaxed where nobody is taking the game all too seriously. Having dbd be a party game is great, a really good way to spend your night with a few friends and just see how it goes.
You can have the new guys, the experiences guys, or anybody in-between still have fun in customs since you are all there wanting to have fun rather than win.

So with all of this said, I am putting the game down and refusing to play the game normally, I will only ever touch the game if 2v8 is back, or my friends decide to play, which really sucks since I really do enjoy the game, but as it stands right now, I just can't enjoy it, I physically cannot enjoy the game in its current state.

Dead by Daylight - a name-based breakdown

[b]Dead[/b]
You play in one of two teams (yes, a solo team is still a team), either trying to do the dead to someone or avoiding becoming the dead.
As the killer, it is your job to find people, run in circles of varying radii while dodging pallets thrown at you for at least 10 minutes, attack survivors with often questionable hit registration, and scramble to find a hook in proximity. Rinse and repeat thrice per survivor.
You also get a large cast of characters with increasingly broken and more abundant abilities and perks (scaling with in-game and IRL money cost, of course).
As a survivor, your job is one of: Holding Mouse Button 1 for an eternity and occasionally tapping space, running in circles of varying radii while dodging the killer, dropping pallets and jumping through windows, and enjoying the scenery while [i]hanging around[/i].

[b]by[/b]
By choosing to play this of your own free will, you prove that you are masochistic.
As the killer, the survivors always find some random junk scattered by a tornado to hide behind, and as a survivor, the killer is always slightly* faster than you.
If you are planning to play a killer with projectile or ranged attacks, dont't. Hitboxes in this game have been proven to protrude into the 7th dimension, especially those that don't look that way.
Conversely, survivors have been known to have been hit by attacks through solid objects.
Really shows how our understanding of physics breaks down beyond the third spatial dimension.
Also remember to pray to RNGsus before running through shrubbery, as it might be of the 'solid' genus despite sharing the phenotype of their 'transparent' siblings.
It's also funny how there are never any windows or pallets while you are being chased. Well, back to admiring the level geometry.

The performance is also abysmal. Lowering the graphics settings barely makes a difference, as the game is consistently gobbling up 80-100% of my CPU even while not much or even nothing is happening (e.g. game lobby, transition screens).
Depending on the map, it turns into a PowerPoint presentation as soon as at least one other player is on screen for no discernable reason.
On a positive note, I no longer have to change settings every time I boot up the game, so a big round of applause.

To put it simply, this game is not fun for 70% of the time you play it, and when it is fun it's only when you're a survivor bullying the killer. Survivors get handheld because the devs want the game to be "beginner friendly" which is a bunch of bs since it means they just buff and buff and buff survivor until it's literally impossible to play against them. To TLDR this review; Survivor is easy and boring, Killer is rage inducing and absolutely not worth your time if you haven't spent money on the game, The devs don't care about anything the community says to help make improvements and instead they push buffing survivor, The community in-game is ass.

[h1] Dead by Daylight is an inconsistent, overpriced mess. [/h1]

For the record, my total playtime across multiple platforms should be around 2000, not the 300 that my profile shows. I played actively from late 2019 to about 2022 or 2023, but have known the game since at least 2017 or 2018. I was a HUGE fan with a lot of passion, but nowadays the game doesn't capture the same magic that it used to. Not saying that dbd was necessarily better back then, of course not! It was a buggy, poorly balanced mess and guess what, it still is today, just less extreme.

To get the elephant in the room out of the way, this game costs you around 20€ upfront, but then has the audacity to charge you up to over 300€ for DLC content. Yes, about half of these can be unlocked in-game, but grinding iridescent shards is tedious. Not as much as it used to be, but it still is. Even then, about half the content is licensed so you'd need to pay around 150€ anyway to get that. On top of that, the game has a battlepass and an in-game store with overpriced cosmetics. This alone is reason enough to stay away from this game honestly.

Now for the actual gameplay though... it's weird.

DbD can surely be fun, but a lot of matches will have you mad at something. This game really knows how to push your buttons. While I am a lot more chill with this game these days, I get why a lot of people get mad at it. Many matches end up extremely one sided, which can be pretty boring and frusttrating. The most lame playstyles are often times the most efficient. So so sooo many perks are also completely useless and not worth running or have a better alternative somewhere else, so you often times see the same loadouts. It used to be much worse, but last time I checked, there's still a lot of stuff that no one really likes to use. Who the hell runs visionary for example???

The Killer roster has also seen better days. Most of the new characters really fail to grab me. Their playstyles are just mixes of multiple abilities that have been executed much better in the past. It's not all that exciting having the 500th character that has a straight forward, mid range, attack. Or having the 500th character that has objects on the map that they can teleport to. It's all been done so many times now that I have little reason to actually play a lot of those Killers, when a more refined and established variant of that character already exists.

Not to mention that half the Killer roster is also not that fun to go against most of the time.

Playing Survivor is most fun with friends usually. When I first started playing Dead by Daylight, I genuinely thought I’d found one of the most exciting multiplayer horror games ever made. The first 100 hours or so were a blast, running from killers with friends, pulling off clutch saves, and feeling that rush of tension as the exit gates opened. But once your MMR starts to climb, that fun quickly evaporates. The game goes from thrilling to downright miserable, and it’s honestly shocking how steep the falloff in enjoyment is.

At higher MMR, the game feels completely unbalanced. Killers suddenly move faster, hit from ridiculous distances, and seem to have a supernatural ability to track you no matter what. The supposed “skill based” matchmaking doesn’t really feel like it takes into account teamwork or playstyle; you just get thrown against sweaty killers with pinpoint accuracy and map knowledge that make most matches feel hopeless.

And the tools survivors get to fight back? Practically useless. Flashlights almost never work properly; you can aim dead on and still get nothing. Pallet stuns feel inconsistent, sometimes they register, other times the killer just powers through like nothing happened. Even perks that are meant to help counter killer pressure barely make a difference at high levels because of how oppressive killer perks and add ons have become.

The worst part is how predictable the experience becomes. If the killer isn’t brand new, they will catch you, it’s only a matter of time. There’s no real comeback potential unless the killer makes a huge mistake or decides to give you a pity escape. That feeling of tension that once made the game fun is replaced by frustration, because it’s not about skill anymore, it’s about how long you can delay the inevitable.

Dead by Daylight has a solid foundation, and for casual players or newcomers, it can still be enjoyable. But for anyone who plays long enough to get decent, the experience becomes punishing and unrewarding. It’s like the game actively punishes you for improving. Until the developers seriously rework MMR and address balance issues between killers and survivors, I can’t recommend it beyond the first few dozen hours. It’s fun until it isn’t. Then it’s just pain.

I would have liked to play the original DBD when it was first released. The maps looked bigger, atmosphere moodier, and it was more about stealth. Sure, the game play experience was minimal and simple. But it felt closer to what the game was originally inspired by: the 80s horror/slasher films where killers are unrelentless pursuers and victims needing to hide and outwit with the fewest of meager resources. Really, who was one of the first licensed IP killers for this game? 

Now, DBD has transitioned into a confusing mess of an arcade game where you need a user manual to know what killer/survivors you are grouped with and what overpowered add-ons they have. The steep learning curve for survivors is so laughable that it makes total sense that most players main as killers in this game. It's almost always 1.5 percent bonus blood points for survivors.
 
Over the years, I wished for bigger/diverse maps and unique generators with different skill checks/challenges. After all, with each new survivor and killer for a chapter, you would expect further commitment towards holistic improvement of the game experience. Instead, I have seen corporate miscommunication, mile-long messages noting latest bug patches/kill switches, and unfulfilled promises. One can say that the game is for "casual" players, but that doesn't excuse it being downright unplayable at times. 

But what do I know? Maybe in this day and age, an obviously broken game can manipulate people to actually think it takes skill and mind games to win when it's easy for players to abuse the game play and ruin the fun. At the end of the day, there are no substantial preventive/counter measures towards ensuring fair play despite the so-called initiative for anti-slugging, anti-camping, and anti-tunneling that were made to address DBD's current rework. And by the way, afk killers don't get penalized but survivors do when they're afk? So a boring free win is acceptable and I get penalized for wanting to leave a stalling match? Am I missing something here?

There were moments when I enjoyed the game and its spooky campy vibes. There aren't a lot of multiplayer games in the horror genre which makes DBD one of the few. But this year, there weren't as many good moments. Yeah, let's all gather around the bonfire one more time and laugh about Jim the Pole, but the charm has faded and the air has gotten stale. 

Time for something new and properly tested.

"Would I recommend Dead by Daylight?"
Absolutely not — but I’ll still be logging in tomorrow.

This game is like an abusive relationship, only with more teabags and even less communication. It pulls you in with promises of fun chases, thrilling escapes, and the occasional dopamine hit when you outsmart a killer, and promises of balancing the game from BHVR. You think, “Maybe it’s different this time. Maybe the playerbase is coming around and getting on the same page that it's supposed to be FUN for all 5 in the lobby." Then it gaslights you; a killer facecamps you, your teammates sandbag you, and somehow you end up thinking it’s your fault. “If I’d just looped better… if I’d brought Dead Hard or Decisive Strike or Unbreakable... or Lightborn (for the killers)..." because that's what BHVR and the sweaty players will tell you. But then you get one amazing match where everyone plays fair, you escape through the gate or hatch, and your brain goes, “See? It’s not that bad.” And just like that, you’re back.

917 hours later, here I am. I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone I care about — but if you do play, welcome to the support group. We meet in the fog.

Dead by Daylight is not an easy or beginner-friendly game by any means. The biggest flaw? It desperately needs an updated tutorial and practice mode. New players have no way to rehearse basic skills like flashlight saves, flash bangs, loops, or facing specific killers. In custom matches, you can only fight bot survivors as killer—never the other way around.

I’ve introduced this game to several friends; 90% quit within their first week. The learning curve is brutal and full of odd mechanics (like having to line up exactly 90° for a fast vault). After nearly a decade, the same issues remain—tunneling and slugging still dominate matches, making the solo experience miserable. Solo queue players are punished by design, since survivors can’t communicate beyond basic gestures (“come here” or “follow me”).

The developers seem to prioritize new content over stability, balance, or beginner accessibility. The business cycle feels predictable: announce a new killer, generate hype, attract new buyers, they realize how unforgiving the game is—and then they leave.

A notable example I would like to point out is Dead by Daylight hasn’t been forced to evolve for nearly 10 years due to lack of major sustainable competition. Until Behaviour Interactive adds quality-of-life features that support new and solo players, I can’t recommend this game to anyone starting fresh.

Verdict: Great concept, deeply flawed execution. 6/10 for veterans, 2/10 for newcomers 

 [Overall]: Not recommended

Christ, what a mess. This game is a lot. Both sides of the coin, killer and survivor will always tell you that the other side is handheld by the developer, the other side is too easy, it's too broken, blah, blah blah. Let me ask you, then. Which side are new players AFRAID to play? Is it the half of the game where they are hunted down like prey, slaughtered while they run and complete objectives? Or is it the one doing the slaughtering, the one holding those lives in the palm of their hands? It's killer. It's always been killer. Because killer has always been the centerpiece of any match of DBD, killer NEEDS to feel good. Killer needs to feel powerful. Killer needs to feel... fun. And recently, it feels like BHVR has been trying their hardest to prevent that from being possible.

 I try my best to leave survivors alone when they get unhooked, unless there's a damn good reason to do otherwise. I've never slugged someone out in my life. And yet, I'm being punished by the devs for the actions of bad actors by having survivors be granted 30 seconds of fucking god mode on unhook. Wicked and Resurgence are going to allow survivors to go down, get hooked in basement, self unhook in front of my face at FULL HEALTH, get hit, run away for 29 seconds, get hit again because they still have endurance, and then make a break for it. The pallet density is still off the charts. And what do killers get for these survivor buffs? One tier of bloodlust. .2 meters per second of movement speed. Most killer's base movement speed is 4.6 meters per second. That is a microscopic increase. And not only is the increase microscopic, it is very fragile. If I'm playing a mid-tier killer, one that is supposed to benefit from this move speed increase instead of making the top tiers stronger, what do you suppose the first thing I'll want to do after hooking a survivor is? Looking for another survivor. How does The Knight do that? Well, it's easy! I'll just send out my guard, check this generator, and... my movement speed bonus is gone. All because I tried to play the game.  How does The Doctor do that? Let me just charge up my static blast, and... the movement speed is gone. Any teleport killer? Gone. Any information? Bye-bye. Stealth? Nope. This is the kind of ass-backwards design that BHVR comes up with to keep the playing field "fair". It's nonsense. 

Let it be known. I'm no fool. BHVR is no stranger to swinging the pendulum the other way. I remember Call of Brine Eruption. I was there for original Hex: Ruin (which was only so universal because survivors were given more tools than killers had at the time, but I digress). Killer has been miserable for survivors to play against too. But that's the problem. This is a fucking video game. Why should we be miserable? Please respect your own.

This is the first game I've ever bought on Steam, and I loved it. I got into the game by watching people like No0b3 and Otzdarva play it all the time when I was younger, and for the collaborations they did with horror icons. I always played killer since I didn't have friends to play survivor with, but I eventually learned to play both at some point. However, I would be lying if I said I enjoyed playing it anymore. 

I don't know if it's the fact that I'm getting older, that I've played more games I enjoy, or if it's the game itself that has changed, but every time I come back to play, there's always something that makes me step away from the game for a while. Whether it's an adjustment to perks making them more broken or useless, bugs and hackers, new mechanics, or even just toxic players, I just can't find a reason to stick around after getting back into the game.

This game is notorious for being an unbalanced mess and having a toxic community. I haven't encountered many toxic people in the game since around 2019, when I started, but I've seen so many toxic people outside the game that it absolutely makes me hate playing. I cannot recommend playing the game at all in its current state. Playing as the survivor or killer is miserable in their own way, and I have played against more hackers than I ever have during the rest of the time I have played this game.

I think you could also argue this game is pay to win in a way, I don't know if I would call it exactly that, but there's definitely a huge advantage you get from buying certain licensed DLC either for the perks or the killer themselves, but I think using them effectively still requires skill although that still doesn't change how unfair killers can be sometimes as much as I love playing them.

Playing survivor is fun and simple for the most part, especially if you're playing with friends or in a group. But I do think there are some problems that you face when playing against certain killers that just aren't fun to play against.

And playing as killer is horrendous. I love playing killer, but it feels like there's a set list of rules you have to follow, or else survivors will just complain about how you played. On top of that, you have to deal with bully squads that just make the whole game about harassing you. I enjoy friendly survivors, but getting them every other match can be annoying. Sometimes I just want to play the game, and then I'm the one at fault when I kill them because they didn't want to play a normal match.

I want this game to do well, but every year I feel like it just gets worse and worse. The only thing keeping it alive for me now is the collaborations they do, but even that is starting to not feel like enough anymore. In its current state, I just can't recommend it to anyone looking to buy it.

Attention all who may be interested in this game,

DO NOT buy this game. You'll get it and think "OMG this is scary and exciting!"... You might even think it's a great game for a while.. but then the curtains will rise...

First you will start playing survivor with your friends, using discord to communicate and scream while still thinking its fun but somehow the killer always catches you or finds you way too quickly. You'll escape a few times and think you did really well. This will go on for a few games but then you will get out of the bot Match Making Rating (MMR), and realize you will only ever go against three (3) killers. Blight, Nurse, and Ghoul... You'll think I just need to learn their quirks and I can probably run them forever. Only 300 hours in and you'll still last only two (2) loops at best against any of those three (3) killers that know what they're doing. You and your friends will grow tired of not having all the perks, and the constant tunneling off hook... the frustration will grow until your friends move on to a non-trash game and thus you are now ready to move to the next phase of self hatred.. Playing killer.

With no friends or good teammates left on this trash game you will phase over to the dark side. At the beginning you'll 4k (kill all 4 survivors) every match or get new players who run in straight lines for instant downs.. you'll think "Oh this is so easy!". Then once again you will get out of the bot MMR and learn the reality.  Endless pallets on large maps and the more than often toxic Survive with Friends (SWF) who communicate with each other the entire game, and will body-block or try and flashlight/pallet save on every single down. Endgame becomes a endless walls of bodies for a down, and you'll start to let the bad thoughts consume you... why shouldn't I play Blight, Nurse, or Ghoul.. I am probably really good at them (you're not) and when you start 4k'ing with the sweatiest perks you can use you'll think.. "Wow I am amazing at this game!" (You are not) and you'll continue the vicious cycle. You'll start to turn on all survivors who are trying their best and realize they are the reason the Dead by Daylight (DBD) community sucks and they are the ones who keep running off their DBD playerbase. Then once that hatred really becomes you.. the process starts over and you go back to survivor.

Once you are empty and returned back to your survivor base... you'll think you know everything there is about killers and start to use every cheesy strategy, perk, and trick that once infuriated you as a killer.. and laugh as they now feel your pain and you start to get out at least 50% of the time... you'll think you are top tier with your 500 hours (you're not) and you'll start being toxic in chat against the same killers you play but now they don't play "fair" by community standards. This soul sucking cycle will then repeat until you have 1000 hours... and then 3000 hours.. There truly won't be a day where you don't hate yourself playing at this point.

If you have made it this far I can now truly tell you the real reason to never play this game. The developers. They are selfish, greedy, and tunnel-visioned. They will look at their #s across all DBD games and translate any high % of perk usage to overpowered and thus needing a nerf. They will add requirements like "must heal someone" or "must be unhooked" or "after 2 downs"... they literally make perks have requirements because they can't balance perk combinations. Then while nerfing both sides they will create bugs that will exist over a span of months, and then fix them only to recreate bugs that existed years before. They will blame the community when they get negative feedback, and they will say the next patch will fix slugging and tunneling (it won't). The real tragedy is these developers don't play the game and when they do they are only as good as bot MMR. Probably modeled the bots after their gameplay, tbh. They don't listen to the community and will continue to kill this game with their ignorance. All while keeping the same three (3) killers buffed, and same meta perks for survivors as the only real options. Fun is not a business model for them, greed and stupidity is what powers Behavior.

Final notes, this game will promise greatness and only succeed in making you hate yourself while making you play again the day after. It's a depressing cycle that never gets better, You'll eventually leave and you'll be better off for it, May it come sooner rather than later. 

Seriously do not buy this game.

I am also an rehabilitated League of Legends addict. I've spent more hours suffering in LoL than I have any other negative experience in my life. I recently escaped my addiction, and somehow replaced it with something worse.

If you are looking for game that is well-maintained, run by a competent developer team, then I would recommend League of Legends before DBD. BHVR have proven time and time again that they do not play their game, and do not actively give a damn about the player base's opinions. This developer team spends more time apologizing to their community than dedicating time to playing the game. Don't trust the developers, play the game for fun, pray they don't shut it down due to sheer incompetence. 

If this game ever dies, it's because BHVR's headquarters got burned down by an angry mob. They actively encourage toxic behavior in their game. Certain gameplay mechanics facilitate community outrage, and recent updates have no Quality Assurance, and add more issues than solutions. Many 'fixes' the developers incorporate only apply to statistics and on paper. They sweep glaring issues under the rug. Cheaters run rampant. In one week alone I encountered a cheater twice a day. That's 14 different cheaters where I only got feedback for reporting one. There is no interesting balancing decisions. The same killer has been S+ tier for her entire existence.

As I stated above, I love the **gameplay** of this game, I love **playing this game with friends** but I do not love this game. I do not love the developers.
